newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end stronger, driven by U.S. gains.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end stronger, driven by U.S. gains.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger after a session of volatile and active trade on Wednesday, taking their cue from the reaction of U.S. treasuries to tame U.S. economic data, analysts said.

"Obviously the news of very weak PPI figures was very well received in spite of the fact that there's still some fairly obvious strength on the consumer spending," said Rich Wylie, fixed-income economist with TD Securities. "Really we've just been sort of riding the coat tails of the U.S. market."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.69 to C$118.74 to yield 6.559 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 16/32 to yield 6.63 percent. The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to seven basis points from eight basis points at Tuesday's close.

Fixed-income markets in both countries strengthened after the U.S. Labor Department said the producer price index fell 0.1 percent in July, compared with expectations of a 0.1 percent rise. The report reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve would keep rates steady this month.
The U.S. Commerce Department also reported this morning that U.S. retail sales rose 0.6 percent in July, below expectations of a 0.7 percent rise.
Dealers said trading volumes were heavy in Canada given the U.S. news and subsequent volatility in the U.S. market.

In provincial trading, Ontario and Ontario Hydro bonds were especially active in today's session, dealers said. Provincially owned Ontario Hydro today announced an overhaul of its nuclear unit, which could cost up to C$8 billion ($5.8 billion) over the next five years.
The utility will therefore not be moving ahead with plans to reduce its debt, now at more than C$30 billion and guaranteed by the province.

Ontario and Ontario Hydro bonds saw spreads to the Government of Canada yield curve widen slightly at the start of the session on the news, but soon returned to previous levels, said Sheldon Dong, head of fixed-income research at Midland Walwyn. Ontario and Ontario Hydro 30-year bonds last traded with a spread of 21 basis points to Canada's long bond.
"I believe this house-cleaning is actually good for Ontario Hydro bonds," said Dong. "I'm viewing this as a long- term positive and I think the market sort of realized that too."
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.77 to C$109.23 to yield 5.981 percent.
The U.S. 10-year bond rose 13/32 to yield 6.35 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 37 basis points from 32 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The 10-year Canadian government bond futures contract trading on the Montreal Exchange closed up 0.49 to 119.57 with 4,043 contracts changing hands, down from 4,558 contracts on Tuesday.
